name: Namibian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Kamei, Nobutaka. 2004. Afurika no shuwa gengo [The sign languages of Africa]. Afurika kenkyu / Journal of African Studies 64: 43-64.
sources.note: Nothing. Continental survey; Namibia receives one sentence: 'ナミビアにはナミビア手話 Namibian Sign Language があり、辞書が編纂された ([EL]; Morgan et al., 1991)' = 'In Namibia there is Namibian Sign Language, and a dictionary has been compiled.' No structural information.

sources.citation: Ashipala, Sackeus P; Profelius, Daniel; Haikali, Marius N; Israel, Nangolo; Linus, Festus T; Niilenge, Henock H; Haiduwah, Timony F; Hashiyanah, Rauna N. 1994. The development of a dictionary of Namibian Sign Language. In Erting, C. et al. (eds), The Deaf Way, 342-346. Washington, DC: Gallaudet University Press. DOI 10.2307/jj.4688148.70
sources.note: Nothing; sociohistorical account of the exile Deaf community (Engela/Eluwa schools, Paget-Gorman origin, Swedish and ASL contact) and of the dictionary method. The JSTOR chapter page itself was not retrievable (error page), but the same paper is reproduced in the 1991 dictionary and was read there.

sources.citation: Morgan, Ruth; Liddell, Scott K; Haikali, Marius M. N; Ashipala, Sackeus P; Daniel, Polo; Haiduwah, Hilifilua E. T; Hashiyana, Rauna N; Israel, Nangolo J; Linus, Festus T; Niilenge, Henock H; Setzer, Paul. 1991. Namibian Sign Language to English and Oshiwambo. Washington, DC: Gallaudet University. xxxv+254 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. The only structural description of NSL in existence: front matter p. xv lists the parameters transcribed for each sign (hand shape, location, orientation, segmental structure, non-manual signals) and Liddell's essay 'The organization of this dictionary' (pp. xxi-xxix) describes simple signs, indicating verbs, locative verbs and classifier verbs. A a full-text search for stress/accent the full 294-page text for stress/accent/prosod/emphasis/intonation/rhythm/syllab returns no hits.

sources.citation: African Sign Languages Resource Center. 'Republic of Namibia' country profile (contributors Heidi Beinhouwer, Michiko Kaneko).https://africansignlanguagesresourcecenter.com/namibia/
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic profile: regional variation per Deaf school (North vs Windhoek); SASL, Swedish SL and ASL influence; dictionaries (1991 onward; NNAD/CCDS online dictionary of ~2000 signs); lists the 1991 dictionary as an open resource at Western Oregon University Digital Commons, which is how the PDF above was located.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page nami1249 and reference records 318904, 552928, 320371, 320035; Wikipedia 'Namibian Sign Language'; Ethnologue 19th ed. archived page for nbs
sources.note: Nothing. Classification (Glottolog: BSL family via SASL; Wikipedia: Paget Gorman), population 8,310 (2008 WFD), status 6a; Glottolog lists no descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference at all.

sources.citation: Wilkinson, Erin Laine. 2009. Typology of signed languages: differentiation through kinship terminology. PhD dissertation, University of New Mexico.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only other academic work Glottolog links to NSL; a cross-sign-language kinship-lexicon survey, so very unlikely to contain a stress statement, but it is the one unopened scholarly item.
